title: Premarket · Monday 10/5

headline.title: Deal day, an election, and a 54% vaccine print. PCVX +54.3% on Phase 3 VAX-31 hitting its endpoints. PTC +35.7% — Schneider at $205, $22.6B. RXO +22.9% on C.H. Robinson's $5.8B offer, with CHRW −8.1% paying for it. And Brazil elected Bolsonaro: XP +18.8%, ITUB +14.3%, NU +12.6%, PBR +10.7%.
headline.summary: Four gaps over 10% and the backtest says the same thing about all of them. Across 19 prior events, every gap of 5% or more closed below its open — 6 of 6. What actually changed on Friday was the rate path: payrolls came in at +29k against ~+90k expected with unemployment up to 4.2%, and October hike odds collapsed into the mid-teens. That is the number carrying into Wednesday's minutes — the committee's lean against a market that has already stopped pricing it.

overview:
Friday was a soft-jobs rally. +29k payrolls against ~+90k expected, unemployment to 4.2%. S&P +0.7% to 7,723, Nasdaq +1.2%. NVDA touched a record $237.87; TSLA +4% on 486.5k deliveries vs ~463k.

October hike odds collapsed into the mid-teens. The 10-year settled near 5.28%, off the prior week's two-decade highs.

Energy has three things at once. The G7 agreed to release 100M barrels of crude and diesel, OPEC+ met Sunday, and the Energy Intelligence Forum opens with the CEOs of Aramco, Eni, BP and TotalEnergies. WTI easing toward $90.50–91.

Upgrades did real work: HOG +5.7% (Citi), DKNG +4.9% — BofA calling prediction markets a “win-win” worth $400M of 2027 fees — EL +3.5%, WFC +1.9%.

Today: ISM Services 9:00, the only data. China closed for Golden Week through Wednesday. Tomorrow: MRVL and ZS investor days, Prime Day one, STZ.

Schneider Electric at $205 a share, $22B equity, closing Q3 2027. Trading 195.50 — a 4.63% spread to the bid. That spread is the whole trade, and it is not a momentum one. A cash price caps it at $205; only a competing bid or a bump pays more. Seven quarters to collect 4.63% is not a $50-risk setup.

Flat at 272.30 into tomorrow's NYC investor day, 8:00 CT. This is the event postponed from June 10, 2025 — 16 months late, which raises the bar. The one comparable, 2024-04-11: a 7.7% range on 1.8x volume, closed +0.14%, then −4.97% over three sessions. That history promises range, not direction.

darkpool.note: Friday's board, and two tickets on it called this morning. SPY printed $1.5B at the bid, the largest on the whole board, with the international pair IDEV $888.0M and IEFA $875.0M behind it. Ex-ETF, MU took the crown again at $489.7M (mixed, AH), then SNPS $427.4M days after its analyst day, META $412.7M (ask), AMGN $406.3M, ORCL $397.8M, COHR $385.1M, QCOM $373.9M (ask), TSLA $345.2M (bid) into its delivery beat, IBM $339.7M (ask) and AAPL $332.8M (ask). Nearly every ticket crossed after hours. Cumulative: SPY $7.4B (bid) leads everything, MU $6.2B (mixed) second on the entire board, NVDA $4.6B, TSLA $2.8B. The call worth noting: Friday's ETF sweep board carried $3.8M of EWZ CALLS — the session before Brazil's election broke market-friendly. This morning the Brazil complex is the entire top of the movers board. That is flow arriving before a dated, binary event, which is the only version of this signal that is worth anything.
darkpool.right_note: The other pairing is VST. The board's largest options ticket Friday was $93.0M of VST PUTS — and this morning VST is +3.2% on a $4B federal nuclear loan package, with its dark pool at the ask and an Outside (3) candle behind it. Into a gap like that, a put block that size reads as a hedge as easily as a bet. Two standing reminders stay on this page: STX's $848M mid print was read here as bearish into +6.93%, and META's candle was read over a catalyst that had not been checked for, into +11.34%.

tts.text: Monday October fifth. Brazil elected Bolsonaro by about two points and the whole complex gapped. E W Z up twelve percent, Itau up fourteen point three, Bradesco up twelve point four. And P T C is up thirty five point seven percent because Schneider Electric is buying it at two hundred five dollars a share, twenty two billion of equity. Two of the biggest gaps on the board this month, both on weekend news, neither on any catalyst calendar. This is the exact setup the backtest just measured. Across nineteen prior events on this week's names, every gap of five percent or more closed below its open. Six of six. Thirteen of nineteen overall. E W Z at twelve percent and P T C at thirty five point seven are the two biggest gaps on the page. P T C has a hard ceiling the others do not. The deal is two hundred five dollars and it is trading one ninety five fifty, a four point six three percent spread that does not close until the third quarter of twenty twenty seven. There is nothing above two oh five except a competing bid. Three things today. First, three upgrades did real work. Harley up five point seven on Citi, Draft Kings up four point nine on Bank of America calling prediction markets a win win worth four hundred million in twenty twenty seven fees, and Estee Lauder up three and a half on Barclays. Second, energy has two events and no direction. Today is the first session after Sunday's O P E C plus meeting, and the two day Energy Intelligence Forum opens with the chief executives of Aramco, Eni, B P and Total Energies all speaking. U S O is down one point three into it. Third, tomorrow is the dense day. Marvell and Zscaler investor days, Prime Big Deal Days opens, and Constellation reports. Marvell's is the event postponed from June of last year, sixteen months late, and its one comparable ran a seven point seven percent range and closed flat, then bled five percent over three sessions. Range, not direction.
